1.title: Chapter 1
1.heading: The slaying of Madhu and Kaitabha, and the appearance of Mahakali
1.summary: King Suratha and the merchant Samadhi come to the hermitage of sage Medha. The sage explains delusion, and through Yoganidra Lord Vishnu awakens and destroys Madhu and Kaitabha.
1.phala: Freedom from mental unrest, depression, nameless fear and confusion.
details: After enemies seized his kingdom, the sorrowing king Suratha reached sage Medha’s hermitage in the forest.
There he met a merchant named Samadhi, whose greedy sons and wife had taken his wealth and driven him from home.
Both asked the sage why their minds still clung to people who had been cruel to them. The sage said this is the power of the Goddess Mahamaya.
At the beginning of creation, during the great dissolution, two mighty demons, Madhu and Kaitabha, arose from the ear-wax of Lord Vishnu.
Brahma praised Yoganidra (Mahakali). By the Mother’s grace the Lord awoke, fought for five thousand years, and slew both demons.

2.title: Chapter 2
2.heading: Mahalakshmi appears from the gods’ radiance, and the generals are destroyed
2.summary: Oppressed by Mahishasura, the gods go to Shiva and Vishnu. From the combined radiance of all the gods, eighteen-armed Mahalakshmi appears and destroys Mahishasura’s army.
2.phala: Victory over enemies, protection of position and honour, and growth of strength and vigour.
details: Mahishasura defeated Indra and the other gods and seized heaven.
A great light came from the faces and limbs of Vishnu, Shiva and all the gods, and the divine Goddess Mahalakshmi appeared.
Shiva gave a trident, Vishnu a discus, Varuna a conch, Agni a spear, and Indra the thunderbolt.
Mahishasura’s generals Chikshura and Chamara attacked with crores of demons. The Mother destroyed them in a moment.

3.title: Chapter 3
3.heading: The slaying of Mahishasura
3.summary: Mahishasura fights by changing into a buffalo, an elephant, a lion and other forms, and at last the Goddess slays him.
3.phala: The end of pride, release from terrible troubles, and peace in the family.
details: Mahishasura took illusory forms and tried to crush the Goddess’s army.
The Mother bound him with a noose and he became a lion. When his head was cut he became a swordsman.
When he became a huge buffalo again, the Mother struck his chest with her trident and cut off his head beneath her foot.

4.title: Chapter 4
4.heading: The hymn of Indra and the gods
4.summary: Indra and the gods praise Mother Jagadamba with devotion, and she promises to protect them whenever they remember her in danger.
4.phala: Great good fortune, the coming of Lakshmi, the wearing away of sin, and the removal of every fear.
details: After Mahishasura was slain, heaven was free of thorns, and the gods praised the Mother with joined hands.
The gods said that whoever honours her with this hymn in devotion will always be protected.

5.title: Chapter 5
5.heading: The Devi Sukta of the gods, and the message of Dhumralochana
5.summary: Tormented by Shumbha and Nishumbha, the gods praise the unconquered Goddess on the Himalaya (Ya Devi sarvabhuteshu). Chanda and Munda send the messenger Sugriva.
5.phala: Learning, intelligence, power of speech, and inner peace.
details: Shumbha and Nishumbha seized the three worlds and took the powers of the Sun, Moon, Yama and Varuna.
The gods went to the Himalaya and praised the Goddess. From Parvati’s body, Kaushiki appeared.
Seeing her matchless beauty, Chanda and Munda told Shumbha to bring the most beautiful woman of the three worlds to his palace.

6.title: Chapter 6
6.heading: The slaying of Dhumralochana
6.summary: The general Dhumralochana, sent by Shumbha with sixty thousand demons, is burned to ash by the Mother’s mere humkara.
6.phala: Quick calming of hostile forces, envy, occult harm and enemies.
details: Dhumralochana insolently tried to carry the Mother away by force.
The Mother’s fierce humkara turned him to a heap of ash, and her lion tore through his army.

7.title: Chapter 7
7.heading: The slaying of Chanda and Munda, and the appearance of Kali
7.summary: Terrifying Kali appears from Ambika’s brow, slays Chanda and Munda, and receives the name Chamunda.
7.phala: Destruction of great fear, doubt, spirit-obstruction and dire danger.
details: Chanda and Munda arrived with a huge army. Anger darkened the Mother’s brow, and from it came dark-faced Kali, holding a sword and a severed head.
Kali devoured elephants, horses and demons, cut off the heads of Chanda and Munda, and offered them to Ambika.

8.title: Chapter 8
8.heading: The slaying of Raktabija
8.summary: The seven Mothers appear — Brahmi, Maheshwari, Kaumari, Vaishnavi, Varahi, Narasimhi and Aindri — and Kali drinks every drop of Raktabija’s blood and slays him.
8.phala: The end of blood disorders, incurable illness, stubborn enemies and family strife.
details: Raktabija’s boon was that every drop of his blood falling on the earth would birth another warrior like him.
Chandi told Kali to spread her mouth and drink every drop, so that no new demon could be born.

9.title: Chapter 9
9.heading: The slaying of Nishumbha
9.summary: Grieving and enraged for his brother, Nishumbha fights a terrible battle and is slain by Mother Durga.
9.phala: Protection from loss of wealth, freedom from debt, and steadiness in livelihood.
details: Nishumbha rained arrows on the Goddess with his army. The Mother cut down his chariot, bow and weapons, and slew him with her trident.

10.title: Chapter 10
10.heading: The slaying of Shumbha, and the Mothers merge back
10.summary: When Shumbha taunts her for fighting with the strength of other women, the Mother draws every Mother-power back into herself and destroys Shumbha alone.
10.phala: Full victory over pride, legal disputes, court cases and social trouble.
details: At Shumbha’s taunt, Brahmi and all the other goddesses merged into Ambika’s pure body.
The Mother lifted Shumbha into the sky, hurled him to the earth, and ended him with her spear.

11.title: Chapter 11
11.heading: The Narayani hymn (Sarvamangala mangalye)
11.summary: After Shumbha is slain, the gods offer the sacred Narayani hymn. The Mother foretells future descents — in Nandagopa’s house, as Bhramari, and as Shakambhari.
11.phala: Fulfilment of wishes, unbroken good fortune, the joy of children, and liberation.
details: This chapter is the very heart of the Durga Saptashati. The Mother promises that whenever demonic obstruction arises in the world, she will descend and destroy the demons.

12.title: Chapter 12
12.heading: The fruit and glory of reciting the Saptashati
12.summary: The Goddess herself describes the unfailing fruit of hearing, singing and reciting this sacred glory.
12.phala: The end of poverty, and freedom from plague, famine, prison and the fear of fire; complete protection.
details: The Mother said that whoever recites her path with a one-pointed mind on the eighth, fourteenth and ninth lunar days will never have Alakshmi dwelling in the home.

13.title: Chapter 13
13.heading: Suratha and the merchant receive boons
13.summary: On a riverbank Suratha and the merchant Samadhi make an earthen image of the Mother and practise austerity for three years. She grants Suratha an unbroken kingdom and the merchant liberating knowledge.
13.phala: The return of lost splendour, position and honour, and deep spiritual peace.
details: As sage Medha taught, King Suratha and the merchant Samadhi meditated on the Goddess and repeated Om Aim Hrim Klim Chamundayai Vichche.
The Mother appeared, pleased. She blessed the king to be Savarni Manu in the next birth, and gave the merchant the knowledge that crosses the ocean of becoming.

kavach.name: Devi Kavach
kavach.desc: The Devi Kavach of the Markandeya Purana, which divinely guards every limb of the body.
kavach.significance: Daily recitation protects from all misfortune, fear, spirit-obstruction and untimely death.
verses: Of this Chandi Kavach, the seer is Brahma, the metre is Anushtubh, and the deity is Chamunda. It is recited for the pleasure of Mother Jagadamba.

First Shailaputri, second Brahmacharini, third Chandraghanta, fourth Kushmanda, fifth Skandamata, sixth Katyayani, seventh Kalaratri, eighth Mahagauri and ninth Siddhidatri — these nine goddesses are famed as the Navadurga.
One who is burning in fire, surrounded by enemies in battle, or who in terrible danger takes refuge in the Goddess, meets no harm in the battle of crisis, nor grief, sorrow or fear.

May Aindri guard me in the east, the fire-deity in the south-east, Varahi in the south, the sword-bearer in the south-west, Varuni in the west, the deer-rider in the north-west, Kaumari in the north, and the spear-bearer in the north-east.

argala.name: Argala Stotra
argala.desc: A great hymn that destroys disease, enemies and poverty, and grants beauty, victory and fame.
argala.significance: Saying “grant me form, grant me victory, grant me fame, slay my foes” at the end of each verse fulfils the heart’s wish.
verses: Jayanti, Mangala, Kali, Bhadrakali, Kapalini, Durga, Kshama, Shiva, Dhatri, Svaha and Svadha — I bow to Mother Jagadamba, known by these names.
Victory to you, Goddess Chamunda. Victory to you, remover of the suffering of beings. Victory to you, all-pervading Goddess Kalaratri. I bow to you.
Slayer of Madhu and Kaitabha, giver of a boon to Brahma — grant me divine form, grant me victory, grant me fame, and destroy the enemies that are desire and anger.
Destroyer of Mahishasura, giver of the highest joy to devotees — Mother, grant me form, victory and fame, and destroy my faults.

keelak.name: Kilaka Stotra
keelak.desc: Composed by Lord Shiva to open the seal, so that the recitation does not remain fruitless.
keelak.significance: By repeating the Kilaka, the mantras of the Saptashati awaken and become effective.
verses: Salutation to Lord Shiva, whose body is pure knowledge, whose divine eyes are the three Vedas, who is the cause of attaining welfare, and who bears the crescent moon on his head.
One who understands this Kilaka and praises the Goddess every day without selfish desire attains the highest welfare and spiritual powers.

kunjika.name: Siddha Kunjika
kunjika.desc: According to the Rudrayamala Tantra, reciting this one stotra alone yields the fruit of the whole Durga Saptashati.
kunjika.significance: A most secret and powerful hymn, which awakens the Navarna mantra at once.
verses: Of this Kunjika stotra the seer is Sadashiva, the metre is Anushtubh, and the deity is Kalika. Aim is the seed, Hrim the power, and Klim the seal. The resolve is to recite it for the fulfilment of one’s wish.
O Goddess, hear the excellent Kunjika stotra. By the power of its mantra the japa of Chandi becomes fruitful.
This recitation does not need a separate kavach, Argala, Kilaka, secret, sukta, meditation, nyasa or worship. By the Kunjika alone one receives the fruit of the Durga path.
It is more secret than the secret, rare even for the gods. O Parvati, keep it as carefully hidden as your own origin.
The Navarna mantra and its enclosure. Speak it slowly, in a clear voice.
Salutation to the Goddess in Rudra’s form, crusher of Madhu, slayer of Kaitabha, slayer of Mahishasura, and destroyer of Shumbha and Nishumbha. Great Goddess, make my japa awake and successful.
Aim is creation, Hrim is protection, Klim is desire. Salutation to Chamunda, slayer of Chanda, granter of boons, and to the mantra-formed Goddess who always gives fearlessness.
With the seed syllables, salutation to Kalika, the goddess of speech, and Bhairavi. O Bhavani, bring me welfare.
Thus, in the Rudrayamala Tantra, in the dialogue of Shiva and Parvati, the Kunjika stotra is complete.

aarti.name: Durga Aarti
aarti.desc: The daily auspicious great aarti of Mother Jagadamba.
aarti.significance: Offering aarti at the end of the path asks pardon for any lack in the worship and brings the Mother’s boundless grace.
verses: Victory to Mother Jagadamba. Vishnu, Brahma and Shiva, lord of the gods, meditate on you every day. Vermilion and a tilak of musk adorn your brow.
Your body shines like gold and you wear red garments. A garland of red flowers is at your throat. Riding a lion, bearing sword and skull-cup, you remove every sorrow of your devotees.
